identity.question: Will OpenAI announce another Millennium Prize solution by December 31, 2026?

source: OpenAI-linked public GitHub repository `openai/math`, CONTENTS.md and history.md. Captured body receipts and prior source evaluation are referenced below; scope notes are based on the repository’s own manuscript descriptions, not a proof audit.

candidate_scope_findings.repository_description: Every Dirichlet L-function, including zeta(s), is claimed zero-free in Re(s)>7/8 (companion material states >11/12). The repository calls this the quasi-Riemann hypothesis; it is a specified zero-free half-plane, not a statement that all nontrivial zeta zeros lie on Re(s)=1/2.

The full BSD leading-term formula is claimed for elliptic curves over Q satisfying a low-Selmer-corank condition (full q-power Selmer corank zero or one for some prime; the separate two-primary result likewise assumes two-power Selmer corank at most one). The described statements are conditional/restricted classes, not an unqualified claim of the full BSD conjecture for all elliptic curves.

candidate_scope_findings.catalog_item: 032, “The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties”
candidate_scope_findings.repository_description: Claims the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication, every dimension/codimension. This is a broad theorem for the stated CM class, not a claim covering all smooth projective complex varieties in the general Hodge conjecture.

catalog_items: Weil classes / Hodge classes on abelian powers
candidate_scope_findings.repository_description: Additional Hodge statements are explicitly restricted to specified K3 loci or abelian varieties with stated dimension/action/polarization conditions.

withdrawal_status.fact: Repository history states a sign error in “Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds” invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument used by two dependent papers; it withdrew that paper, “Algebraicity of Kuga–Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces,” and “The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces.” The history says withdrawn papers carry notices and archived versions. This is not the same title as catalog item 032 (CM abelian varieties). The same history says the Oct7 edits to “Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank” removed an obsolete introductory citation, and that other manuscripts received repairs/clarifications; repository statements only.

officiality_and_limits: Existing source packet records OpenAI’s Oct6 math announcement as linking to openai/math; the ordinary direct OpenAI page GET was HTTP403, so its response capture is not the article body. Do not describe the repo itself as a direct OpenAI newsroom response without this link context.

Repository catalog abstracts and history are author-supplied claims; this pass did not inspect full manuscripts or validate proofs. It did not establish any OpenAI public announcement that a general named Millennium problem was solved.

A catalog title/string search is not exhaustive proof that no qualifying announcement exists under another title or in a later statement. Contract requires an announcement that OpenAI solved a named listed problem; restricted theorem scope alone should not be silently equated with the unrestricted prize problem.
